title: Mathematical modeling reveals quantitative properties of KEAP1-NRF2 signaling.
authors: Liu, Shengnan; Pi, Jingbo; Zhang, Qiang
one_liner_zh: 该文用数学建模研究KEAP1-NRF2信号通路定量特性，虽涉及蛋白互作但非DNA结合，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题TF-DNA互作无关。
abstract: Under oxidative and electrophilic stresses, cells launch an NRF2-mediated transcriptional antioxidant program. The activation of NRF2 depends on a redox sensor, KEAP1, which promotes the ubiquitination and degradation of NRF2. While a great deal has been learned about this duo, its quantitative signaling properties are largely unexplored. Here we examined these properties, including half-life, maximal activation, and response steepness (ultrasensitivity) of NRF2, through mathematical modeling. The models describe the binding of KEAP1 and NRF2 via ETGE and DLG motifs, NRF2 production, KEAP1-dependent and independent NRF2 degradation, and perturbations by different classes of NRF2 activators. Simulations revealed at the basal condition, NRF2 is sequestered by KEAP1 and the KEAP1-NRF2 complex is distributed comparably in an ETGE-bound (open) state and an ETGE and DLG dual-bound (closed) state. When two-step ETGE binding is considered, class I-V, electrophilic NRF2 activators shift the balance to a closed state incompetent to degrade NRF2, while the open and closed KEAP1-NRF2 complexes transition from operating in cycle mode to equilibrium mode. Ultrasensitive NRF2 activation (a steep rise of free NRF2) can occur when NRF2 nearly saturates KEAP1. The ultrasensitivity results from zero-order degradation through DLG binding and protein sequestration through ETGE binding. Optimal abundances of cytosolic and nuclear KEAP1 exist to maximize ultrasensitivity. These response characteristics do not require disruption of DLG binding as suggested by the hinge-latch hypothesis. In comparison, class VI NRF2 activators cause a shift to the open KEAP1-NRF2 complex and ultimately its complete dissociation, resulting in a fast release of NRF2 followed by stabilization. However, ultrasensitivity is lost due to decreasing free KEAP1 abundance. In summary, by simulating the dual role of KEAP1, i.e., sequestering and promoting degradation of NRF2, our modeling provides novel quantitative insights into NRF2 activation, which may help design novel NRF2 modulators and understand the oxidative actions of environmental stressors.
abstract_zh: 在氧化和亲电应激条件下，细胞启动由NRF2介导的转录抗氧化程序。NRF2的激活依赖于氧化还原传感器KEAP1，后者促进NRF2的泛素化和降解。尽管关于这一对蛋白质已有大量研究，但其定量信号特性在很大程度上尚未被探索。在此，我们通过数学建模研究了这些特性，包括NRF2的半衰期、最大激活程度和响应陡度（超敏感性）。模型描述了KEAP1与NRF2通过ETGE和DLG基序的结合、NRF2的产生、KEAP1依赖性和非依赖性NRF2降解，以及不同类别NRF2激活剂的扰动。模拟结果显示，在基础条件下，NRF2被KEAP1隔离，且KEAP1-NRF2复合物在ETGE结合（开放）状态和ETGE与DLG双重结合（闭合）状态之间分布相当。当考虑两步ETGE结合时，I-V类亲电性NRF2激活剂将平衡转向无法降解NRF2的闭合状态，而开放和闭合的KEAP1-NRF2复合物从循环模式转变为平衡模式。超敏感的NRF2激活（游离NRF2的陡峭上升）可在NRF2几乎饱和KEAP1时发生。超敏感性源于通过DLG结合的零级降解和通过ETGE结合的蛋白质隔离。细胞质和核内KEAP1存在最佳丰度以最大化超敏感性。这些响应特性不需要如铰链-闩锁假说所建议的那样破坏DLG结合。相比之下，VI类NRF2激活剂导致向开放KEAP1-NRF2复合物的转变，并最终使其完全解离，导致NRF2快速释放随后稳定。然而，由于游离KEAP1丰度的降低，超敏感性丧失。总之，通过模拟KEAP1的双重角色，即隔离和促进NRF2降解，我们的建模为NRF2激活提供了新的定量见解，这可能有助于设计新型NRF2调节剂并理解环境应激源的氧化作用。
